definition: A red ochre or other colored marking substance, especially one rubbed on a ram’s breast so that the ewes he serves are marked; by extension, to mark in this way.
etymology: In Middle English, raddle named red ochre. The word probably grew from the Old English family of read, “red”: first the earth-color, then the sheep farmer’s practical paint.
usage: As the breeding season begins, the shepherd raddles the ram, so each newly marked ewe tells her own small calendar story.
